title: Which Reluctant Believer Are You?
subtitle: Half-convinced, a little suspicious, still showing up. You're in good company.

questions.text: When someone tells you God is real and good, what happens inside you?

options.text: I want proof I can test, not just a feeling.
I'd have to see it with my own eyes to buy it.
I'm curious, but I'd rather ask my questions privately.
Sure. Right. Can anything that good really come my way?

questions.text: What's holding your faith back the most right now?

options.text: Life turned bitter, and I'm not pretending it didn't.
I half believe and half don't, and I'm tired of faking the rest.
I need a sign before I'll commit to anything.
Everyone else seems sure. I want the evidence first.

questions.text: How do you usually explore your questions about God?

options.text: Quietly, after hours, where no one's watching.
Out loud, bluntly, even if it sounds skeptical.
By asking for confirmation again and again.
By admitting honestly that I'm stuck between belief and doubt.

questions.text: Which prayer feels most like yours?

options.text: If this is really You, prove it to me one more time.
Show me. I have to see it before I trust it.
I do believe. Please help the part of me that doesn't.
Just call me bitter, because that's how I feel.

questions.text: Someone invites you to actually meet Jesus for yourself. Your first move?

options.text: I go and look, ready to be unimpressed.
I'd come, but at night, where it's safer to wonder.
I want a guarantee before I show up.
I'm too worn down to expect much.

questions.text: What does your suspicion usually sound like?

options.text: Things this good don't come from a place like that.
I'll believe it when I can touch it.
I have real questions, and I'm not satisfied with easy answers.
I used to hope. Hope cost me too much.

questions.text: When life falls apart, what rises in you?

options.text: A hardness. Don't call me by my old hopeful name anymore.
A need for one more sign that I'm not on my own.
A raw honesty. I believe, sort of, and I'm hurting.
A pull to go ask hard questions in private.

questions.text: What would actually move you closer to trust?

options.text: God being patient with my fear instead of scolding it.
An encounter so real I couldn't explain it away.
Being known by name before I even said a word.
Room to ask everything without being shamed.

questions.text: Deep down, what do you secretly hope is true?

options.text: That my honest, cracked faith is still enough for Him.
That the bitterness isn't the end of my story.
That something genuinely good really did come for me.
That He won't get tired of reassuring a fearful heart.

gideon.name: Gideon (test it twice)
gideon.description: You're not arrogant in your hesitation. You're scared, and you keep asking God to confirm it just one more time before you move. Gideon did exactly that, twice, laying out a fleece, and God answered both times without a trace of irritation. He is gentle with a fearful heart that genuinely wants to obey. He won't run out of patience with you.

scripture.text: And the angel of Jehovah appeared unto him, and said unto him, Jehovah is with thee, thou mighty man of valor.

thomas.name: Thomas (show me)
thomas.description: You won't fake a faith you don't feel, and you'd rather say it plainly than nod along. Thomas wanted to see the wounds for himself, and watch what Jesus did. He didn't shame the doubt. He showed up and held out His hands. Your demand for something real isn't a wall. It's often the very door Jesus walks through to reach you.

scripture.text: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and see my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and put it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.

nicodemus.name: Nicodemus (come at night)
nicodemus.description: You have real questions, and you'd rather bring them quietly than perform certainty in public. Nicodemus came to Jesus after dark, cautious and curious at once, and Jesus met him with one of the most famous conversations in Scripture. Your private wondering is welcome. He isn't waiting for you to have it all figured out before you knock.

scripture.text: Nicodemus saith unto him, How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb, and be born?

naomi.name: Naomi (call me Mara, I'm bitter)
naomi.description: Life took more than you expected, and you've stopped pretending otherwise. Naomi came home empty and told everyone to call her Mara, which means bitter. She wasn't punished for that honesty. Her story quietly turned, through a daughter-in-law's love and a redeemer she never saw coming. Your bitterness is allowed to be spoken, and it doesn't get the last word.

scripture.text: And Ruth said, Entreat me not to leave thee, and to return from following after thee, for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge; thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God;

mark-9-father.name: The Mark 9 Father (I believe, help me)
mark-9-father.description: You carry belief and doubt in the very same breath, and you're brave enough to admit both. That desperate father's prayer might be the most honest line in the whole Bible: I do believe, help my unbelief. And Jesus answered it on the spot. You don't need a flawless faith to come to Him. You just need to bring the cracked one you actually have.

scripture.text: Straightway the father of the child cried out, and said, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.

nathanael.name: Nathanael (can anything good come?)
nathanael.description: You lead with a raised eyebrow. Can anything that good really come from a place like that, or for someone like me? Nathanael said almost those exact words, and then Jesus told him He'd seen him before they ever met. The skeptic became a follower in one sentence. Your bluntness isn't a problem. He sees you behind it, and He likes what He sees.

scripture.text: Nathanael saith unto him, Whence knowest thou me? Jesus answered and said unto him, Before Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.
